scope: Theorem 6.1 of the manuscript “Scalar Potentials and Slow Clocks for Forced Fluid Computation” (preprints/Scalar-Potentials-and-Slow-Clocks-for-Forced-Fluid-Computation-September-27-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 82005335f0aac60f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 11. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For fixed computable ν > 0, every deterministic one-tape machine and finite input effectively determine a smooth mean-zero force on the unit torus, with zero initial velocity, such that ∥∂j t Dα x f(t)∥∞ ≤ Cj,α(1 + t)−1−j for every j, α. The unique global smooth velocity satisfies the same bounds. Its particle from (1/4, 1/2, 1/2) enters {1/2 < x1 < 1} exactly when the machine halts. One choice of force has pressure zero; projecting that force gives a divergence-free choice with the same velocity and a changed normalized pressure. For a fixed machine, the repeated motion before the clock change is independent of the input; only its initial loading motion changes.
